passages.text: Over the last decade, beehives have appeared on the roofs of hotels, schools and even opera houses in many European cities. The people who look after them argue that cities suit bees surprisingly well: parks, gardens and balconies offer a long flowering season, and urban plants are rarely treated with the strong chemicals used on farmland. Honey produced in the middle of a capital city is now sold as a local speciality. Some researchers, however, are uneasy about the trend. A city can feed only a limited number of insects, and every new hive of honeybees competes for the same flowers as wild bees, many of which are already in decline. These scientists do not want the hives removed; they simply point out that planting more flowers would help far more species than adding more hives would.

For a long time, an afternoon nap was regarded as a sign of laziness. Recent work in sleep laboratories has changed that view. In a typical experiment, volunteers learn a list of word pairs in the morning and are tested at the end of the day. Those who sleep for twenty minutes after lunch remember noticeably more pairs than those who stay awake, even though both groups spend the same amount of time studying. The explanation seems to be that during sleep the brain replays and files away what has just been learned. The benefit, however, disappears if the nap is too long: sleepers who are woken after an hour often need half an hour to think clearly again, and their scores are no better than those of the volunteers who did not sleep at all.

Twenty years ago the night train seemed to be disappearing from Europe. Cheap flights had taken most of the passengers, and one company after another closed its sleeper services. Today the picture is different. New routes link Vienna to Paris, Berlin to Stockholm and Zurich to Amsterdam, and tickets for them often sell out weeks in advance. Part of the reason is environmental: a journey by sleeper produces a small fraction of the carbon dioxide released by the same journey by plane. Yet passengers mention practical advantages just as often. A night on a train saves the price of a hotel room, and travellers arrive in the centre of a city rather than at an airport far outside it. The main obstacle is no longer demand but equipment: modern sleeping carriages are expensive, and the factories that build them have long waiting lists.

Seagrass meadows are among the least noticed habitats in the sea. Unlike coral reefs, they attract few tourists, and for years they were dismissed as empty green fields under the water. Marine biologists now describe them very differently. A single hectare of healthy seagrass can shelter thousands of young fish, and the roots hold the sandy seabed together so firmly that they reduce the damage storms cause along the coast. Seagrass also stores carbon in the mud beneath it, and it does so several times faster than a forest of the same size. The bad news is that these meadows are shrinking, mainly because of pollution from farms and from building work near the shore. Restoring them is slow work: the seeds must be collected by hand, and a replanted meadow may need ten years before it functions like a natural one.

In a repair cafe, visitors bring a broken toaster, a torn coat or a bicycle with a flat tyre, and volunteers help them mend it over a cup of coffee. The first of these workshops opened in Amsterdam in 2009; there are now thousands of them worldwide. Their founders insist that the aim is not simply to save objects from the bin. Many visitors have never been shown how to use a screwdriver or a needle, and the volunteers teach as much as they repair. Even so, the movement has run into a familiar obstacle. A growing number of devices are glued rather than screwed together, spare parts are sold only to authorised dealers, and repair manuals are not published at all. Campaigners argue that manufacturers should be obliged to make parts and instructions available, and several governments have begun to introduce rules of this kind.

questions.stem: Because the new wing of the museum was designed with wide corridors and low display cases, ----.

options.o1: visitors in wheelchairs can now reach every exhibit without asking for help
options.o2: the architect had studied in Rome for several years before the project began
options.o3: the oldest part of the building was completed in the middle of the nineteenth century
options.o4: most museums in the country still charge an entrance fee at the weekend
options.o5: the collection includes a number of paintings that were donated last year

questions.trap_note: Müzeyle ilgili doğru görünen bir bilgi verir ama neden-sonuç bağlantısı kurmaz; konu birliği ile mantıksal sonuç karıştırılır.

questions.stem: Although the town council promised to repair the coastal path last spring, ----.

options.o5: many visitors say that the view from the cliffs is the best in the region

questions.why: Although zıt bir devam ister: söz verilmesine rağmen işin hâlâ başlamamış olması, tek karşıtlık ilişkisi kuran seçenektir.
questions.trap_note: Aynı haftaya ait ikinci bir habere geçer; also ile kurulan bu ekleme ilişkisi, Although'un istediği karşıtlığı vermez.

questions.stem: The storm on Tuesday night was so violent ----.

options.o1: that half the village was left without electricity until the following afternoon
options.o2: because the roofs of several houses were damaged by falling branches
options.o3: so the ferry service to the island was cancelled for two days
options.o4: although the forecast had warned people about it the previous evening
options.o5: which left the harbour road completely blocked with sand

questions.why: so + sıfat kalıbı yalnızca that ile tamamlanır; böylece şiddetin sonucu verilir.
questions.trap_note: Anlamca makul bir sonuç verdiği için çekicidir, ancak so ... so biçiminde aynı bağlacı tekrarlayarak yapıyı bozar.

questions.stem: It was such a well-organised conference ----.

options.o1: that even the sessions starting at eight in the morning were crowded
options.o2: because the organisers had worked on the programme for a whole year
options.o3: so the participants asked for a similar event the following spring
options.o4: while some of the speakers arrived directly from the airport
options.o5: which the university now wants to host every September

questions.why: such a + sıfat + isim kalıbının karşılığı that yan cümlesidir ve sonucu bildirir.
questions.trap_note: Konferansın neden iyi düzenlendiğini açıkladığı için doğru görünür; oysa such ... that yapısı sebep değil sonuç ister.

questions.stem: Having spent three weeks in the mountains without an internet connection, ----.

questions.trap_note: Anlamca uygun görünür ama öznesi there'dır; bu da sarkık ortaç (dangling modifier) hatası doğurur.

questions.trap_note: Araya giren on the top floor of the library öbeği yüzünden fiili tekil çeker; özne-yüklem uyumu bozulur.

questions.stem: Babası yıllarca bu fabrikada çalışmış olan mühendis, üretim hattını yeniden tasarlamakla görevlendirildi.

options.o2: The engineer who his father had worked in this factory for years was assigned to redesign the production line.

options.o4: The engineer whose father had worked in this factory for years assigned the production line to be redesigned.
options.o5: The father of the engineer, who had worked in this factory for years, was assigned to redesign the production line.

questions.trap_note: Görevlendirileni mühendisin babası yapar; ilgi cümlesinin ait olduğu ad değişince cümlenin öznesi kayar.

questions.stem: According to the passage, the people who keep bees in cities claim that ----.

options.o1: the flowering season there is long and city plants are less exposed to strong chemicals
options.o2: the roofs of large buildings are the only places where hives are really safe
options.o3: honey from a city centre brings in more money than honey from farmland
options.o4: wild bees have already disappeared from most urban parks and gardens
options.o5: city councils treat their parks with chemicals that are harmless to insects

questions.why: Parçada arıcıların gerekçesi açıkça verilir: parklar ve balkonlar uzun bir çiçeklenme mevsimi sunar ve kentteki bitkilere tarım arazilerindeki güçlü kimyasallar nadiren uygulanır.
questions.trap_note: 'Nadiren güçlü kimyasal uygulanır' ifadesini 'zararsız kimyasallar kullanılır' diye okur; sıklık bildiren bir ifade, kesin bir iddiaya dönüştürülür.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that the researchers mentioned in it ----.

options.o1: do not object to urban hives in themselves but question how much they help bees in general
options.o2: want the hives on city buildings to be taken down as soon as possible
options.o3: believe that honeybees and wild bees never feed on the same flowers
options.o4: have proved that wild bees are declining because of the hives on city roofs
options.o5: are mainly interested in improving the quality of honey produced in cities

questions.why: Parça, bilim insanlarının kovanların kaldırılmasını istemediğini, yalnızca daha çok çiçek ekmenin daha yararlı olacağına dikkat çektiğini söyler.
questions.trap_note: Rekabet gözlemini kanıtlanmış bir neden-sonuç ilişkisine dönüştürür; parçada geçen 'competes' ile 'proved ... because of' aynı şey değildir.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the number of flowers in a city ----.

options.o1: sets a limit on the number of bees that the city is able to support
options.o2: has risen steadily since the first hives appeared on the roofs
options.o3: is greater in capital cities than it is in farming areas
options.o4: matters less than the number of hives that are installed
options.o5: is decided mainly by the owners of the hotels and schools

questions.why: 'Bir şehir yalnızca sınırlı sayıda böceği besleyebilir' cümlesi, sınırı belirleyenin besin, yani çiçek miktarı olduğu çıkarımını verir.
questions.trap_note: Parçadaki tek karşılaştırma kimyasallarla ilgilidir; ima edilen karşılaştırma, söylenmiş bir karşılaştırma gibi ele alınır.

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.o1: Keeping bees in cities has become popular, but more hives do not necessarily mean more bees.
options.o2: Honey produced in city centres tastes better than honey produced in the countryside.
options.o3: Wild bees are disappearing all over Europe because of modern farming methods.
options.o4: Opera houses and hotels have become the most important centres of urban agriculture.
options.o5: Scientists and beekeepers rarely agree on the way insects should be protected.

questions.why: Parça önce kent arıcılığının yaygınlaşmasını, sonra da bunun arı çeşitliliğine katkısına dair kuşkuları anlatır; ana düşünce bu iki yarıyı birlikte kapsar.
questions.trap_note: Metindeki tek bir görüş ayrılığını 'nadiren anlaşırlar' biçiminde genelleştirir; ayrıntıdan yapılan aşırı genelleme ana fikir sanılır.

questions.stem: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.

options.o1: the effect of a short afternoon sleep on the ability to remember new material
options.o2: the reasons why people used to regard afternoon naps as a sign of laziness
options.o3: the differences between sleep laboratories and ordinary classrooms
options.o4: the amount of time volunteers need in order to learn a list of word pairs
options.o5: the difficulties faced by people who are unable to sleep during the day

questions.why: Parçanın tamamı kısa uykunun hatırlama üzerindeki etkisini ölçen deneyleri ve bu etkinin sınırını anlatır.
questions.trap_note: Yalnızca ilk cümleye dayanır; giriş cümlesindeki eski görüş, parçanın konusu sanılır.

questions.stem: According to the passage, the volunteers who slept for twenty minutes ----.

options.o1: recalled more word pairs than those who stayed awake, though both groups studied for the same time
options.o2: were given more time to study the word pairs than the other group was
options.o3: were tested immediately after waking up rather than at the end of the day
options.o4: reported that they had found the word pairs easier to learn than usual
options.o5: did just as well as the volunteers who had slept for a whole hour

questions.why: Parça, yirmi dakika uyuyanların uyanık kalanlardan belirgin biçimde daha fazla kelime çifti hatırladığını ve iki grubun aynı süre çalıştığını söyler.
questions.trap_note: Bir saat uyuyanların puanının hiç uyumayanlarla aynı olduğu bilgisini, yirmi dakika uyuyanlara taşır; iki farklı grubun sonuçları birbirine karıştırılır.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that a nap lasting about an hour ----.

options.o3: makes volunteers forget the word pairs they have learned in the morning
options.o4: is harmful only when it is taken immediately after lunch
options.o5: leaves sleepers unable to concentrate for the rest of the day

questions.trap_note: 'Daha iyi değil' ifadesini 'daha kötü, unutturuyor' diye okur; eşitlik bildiren bir ifade, kayıp bildiren bir ifadeye çevrilir.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that researchers explain the effect of the short nap by referring to ----.

options.o1: the way the sleeping brain deals with information that has just been learned
options.o2: the extra energy that volunteers gain from resting after a meal
options.o3: the quiet conditions that are provided in sleep laboratories
options.o4: the motivation of volunteers who agree to take part in experiments

questions.why: Parçadaki açıklama açıktır: uyku sırasında beyin yeni öğrenilenleri tekrar oynatır ve yerleştirir.
questions.trap_note: Öğle yemeği sonrası dinlenmeyi enerji kazanımı gibi yorumlar; parçada geçmeyen, gündelik sezgiye dayalı bir gerekçedir.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that sleeper services in Europe ----.

questions.stem: According to the passage, seagrass meadows were ignored for many years because ----.

options.o1: they were taken to be lifeless areas of no particular interest
options.o2: they were too deep for marine biologists to study properly
options.o3: they grew only in places that tourists were unable to reach
options.o4: they were believed to store far less carbon than forests did
options.o5: the fish sheltering in them were of little commercial value

questions.why: Parça, çayırların yıllarca 'su altındaki boş yeşil tarlalar' sayılarak önemsenmediğini söyler.
questions.trap_note: Karbon karşılaştırmasını tersine çevirir; parçada çayırların ormandan daha hızlı depoladığı yazılıdır.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that the roots of seagrass ----.

options.o1: protect the coast by holding the sandy seabed in place
options.o2: grow more quickly than the roots of forest trees do
options.o3: are damaged mostly by the fish that shelter among them
options.o4: stop the farms near the shore from polluting the water
options.o5: make it impossible for storms to reach the coast at all

questions.why: Kökler kumlu deniz tabanını sıkıca tuttuğu için fırtınaların kıyıda yol açtığı zarar azalır.
questions.trap_note: 'Zararı azaltır' ifadesini 'fırtınaların ulaşmasını imkânsız kılar' biçiminde mutlaklaştırır; derece bildiren bir ifade kesinlik bildiren bir ifadeye çevrilir.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that a newly replanted seagrass meadow ----.

options.o1: does not provide the benefits of an established meadow straight away
options.o2: grows faster than a meadow that has never been damaged
options.o3: can survive only if tourists are kept away from it
options.o4: stores more carbon in its first years than it does later on
options.o5: is normally planted by machines rather than by hand

questions.why: Yeniden ekilen bir çayırın doğal bir çayır gibi işlev görmesi için on yıla ihtiyaç duyabilmesi, yararların hemen ortaya çıkmadığı anlamına gelir.
questions.trap_note: Tohumların elle toplandığı bilgisini görmezden gelir; parçada açıkça yazan ayrıntının tersini söyler.

questions.stem: The main point the writer makes about seagrass meadows is that ----.

options.o1: they are far more valuable than they look, and yet they are being lost
options.o2: they are the only habitat in the sea that is able to store carbon
options.o3: they ought to be protected because tourists have started to visit them
options.o4: they will recover by themselves once pollution from farms is reduced
options.o5: they matter more to marine biology than coral reefs do

questions.why: Parça çayırların fark edilmeyen değerini sıralar, ardından bu değerin kirlilik yüzünden kaybedildiğini söyler; ana düşünce bu karşıtlıktır.
questions.trap_note: Parçadaki tek mercan karşılaştırması turist ilgisiyle ilgilidir; ima edilen bir karşılaştırma, kurulmuş bir karşılaştırma gibi okunur.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that the founders of repair cafes ----.

options.o1: regard the teaching of practical skills as no less important than mending objects
options.o2: believe that most household devices cannot be repaired at all
options.o3: originally intended their workshops to be ordinary cafes
options.o4: expect visitors to bring their own tools and spare parts
options.o5: are mainly interested in reducing the price of new appliances

questions.why: Kurucuların amacın yalnızca eşyaları kurtarmak olmadığını vurgulaması ve gönüllülerin tamir ettikleri kadar öğretmeleri, öğretmenin eşit ağırlıkta olduğunu gösterir.
questions.trap_note: Addaki 'cafe' sözcüğüne takılır; mekânın adı, kuruluş amacı sanılır.

questions.stem: According to the passage, one of the difficulties the repair movement faces is that ----.

options.o1: manufacturers do not make spare parts and repair manuals widely available
options.o2: volunteers are not allowed to work on electrical devices
options.o3: the number of such workshops has fallen sharply since 2009
options.o4: visitors are unwilling to pay for the parts that they need
options.o5: governments have refused to take any interest in the problem

questions.why: Parça engeli açıkça sayar: yedek parçalar yalnızca yetkili satıcılara verilir ve tamir kılavuzları hiç yayımlanmaz.
questions.trap_note: Parçanın son cümlesiyle çelişir; birkaç hükûmetin bu yönde kural getirmeye başladığı yazılıdır.

questions.stem: It is clear from the passage that products which are glued together ----.

options.o1: are harder to take apart and mend than products held together with screws
options.o2: last considerably longer than products held together with screws
options.o3: are no longer produced in most of the countries of Europe
options.o4: can be repaired only by the people who designed them
options.o5: were the reason why the first repair cafe was opened

questions.why: Yapıştırılmış cihazlar, hareketin karşılaştığı engeller arasında sayılır; yani sökülüp onarılmaları vidalı olanlara göre zordur.
questions.trap_note: Yedek parçanın yalnızca yetkili satıcılara satıldığı bilgisini 'yalnızca tasarımcıları onarabilir' biçiminde abartır.

questions.stem: The passage is mainly about ----.

options.o1: a growing movement to repair everyday objects and the obstacles that it meets
options.o2: the history of the city of Amsterdam as a centre of design
options.o3: the reasons why household appliances break down so often
options.o4: the training that volunteers must complete before joining a workshop
options.o5: new laws that have made the repair of devices illegal in some countries

questions.why: Parçanın ilk yarısı hareketin yayılmasını, ikinci yarısı ise karşılaştığı engelleri anlatır.
questions.trap_note: Son cümledeki düzenlemeleri tersine çevirir; tamiri kolaylaştıracak kurallar, tamiri yasaklayan kurallar sanılır.

dialogue: I see that the university has finally put bicycles at the main gate. Have you tried them?
Twice, actually. They are free for the first half hour, and that is enough to get to the science campus.
No, you register once with your student card, and after that you simply unlock a bike with your phone.

options.o1: Do you have to book one in advance every time you want to ride?
options.o2: How long does it take to walk from the main gate to the science campus?
options.o3: Are the bicycles kept inside the library building at night?
options.o4: Why did the university decide to buy so many bicycles at once?
options.o5: Does the university charge the staff more than it charges students?

questions.why: Selin'in 'Hayır, bir kez kayıt oluyorsun' yanıtı, ancak her seferinde rezervasyon gerekip gerekmediğini soran bir cümleyi karşılayabilir.
questions.trap_note: Konuyla ilgilidir ve evet/hayır sorusudur; ancak yanıttaki kayıt ve telefonla açma açıklamasıyla mantıksal bağı yoktur.

dialogue: Your museum has started to stay open late on Fridays. Whose idea was that?
It came from the visitors themselves. In a survey last year, a third of them said they could not come during working hours.
Not at all. Friday evenings are now the busiest hours of our whole week.

options.o1: And has the change turned out to be a disappointment in terms of visitor numbers?
options.o2: Are you planning to close the museum on Mondays instead?
options.o3: Was the survey carried out by an independent company?
options.o4: How many people took part in that survey altogether?
options.o5: Are the evening visitors mostly tourists from abroad?

questions.why: 'Hiç de değil. Cuma akşamları haftanın en yoğun saatleri' yanıtı, ancak uygulamanın hayal kırıklığı olup olmadığını soran bir cümleyi izleyebilir.
questions.trap_note: Akşam ziyaretçileriyle ilgilidir, ama yanıtı 'hiç de değil' olan bir soru değildir; ziyaretçi profili ile yoğunluk karıştırılır.

dialogue: I have to give a fifteen-minute presentation next week and I am terrified.
Everyone feels like that at first. What worries you more, the talk itself or the questions at the end?
Then write your first two sentences word for word and learn them by heart. Once you have started, the rest usually follows.

options.o1: The opening, I think. I never know how to begin without sounding nervous.
options.o2: The questions, of course. I can never predict what the audience will ask.
options.o3: Neither, really. My problem is that the slides are not ready yet.
options.o4: Both of them, but mostly the fact that the lecture room is so large.
options.o5: Actually, I have decided to ask for a different date for the presentation.

questions.why: Eğitmenin ilk iki cümleyi ezberleme önerisi, yalnızca konuşmaya başlamanın sorun olduğu bir yanıttan sonra anlamlıdır.
questions.trap_note: Sorudaki iki seçenekten diğerini işaretler; sorunun soruluş biçimine uygun olsa da eğitmenin yanıtıyla bağdaşmaz.

dialogue: Your company has stopped printing paper catalogues after forty years. Was that not a risky decision?
We hesitated for a long time. In the end the figures decided it for us: nine out of ten orders were already coming through the website.
Some did, yes. That is why we still send a short printed list to any customer who asks for one.

options.o1: Did the older customers who preferred the catalogue object to the change?
options.o2: How much money did the company save in the first year?
options.o3: Was the website redesigned before the catalogue was withdrawn?
options.o4: Do your competitors still produce printed catalogues?
options.o5: Which of your products sell best through the online shop?

questions.why: 'Bazıları itiraz etti, evet' yanıtı ve ardından gelen basılı liste açıklaması, ancak müşterilerin tepkisini soran bir cümleyi karşılar.
questions.trap_note: Basılı katalogla ilgilidir ama öznesi rakip firmalardır; 'Some did' zamiri karşılıksız kalır.

dialogue: There is a notice on the door saying that the lift will be out of service for three days.
Yes, they are replacing the cables. Apparently it has not been done since the building was finished.
I asked about that. They said they would carry the shopping upstairs for anyone living on the top floors.

options.o1: What about Mrs Demir on the sixth floor? She can hardly manage the stairs.
options.o2: Do you happen to know whether the new cables were expensive?
options.o3: I only hope the workers will not start too early in the morning.
options.o4: Has anyone told the residents on the ground floor about the notice?
options.o5: Perhaps we should ask them to paint the staircase as well.

questions.why: Alışverişin üst katlara taşınacağı yanıtı, ancak merdiven çıkamayan bir üst kat sakini gündeme getirildiğinde anlam kazanır.
questions.trap_note: Aynı ilanla ilgilidir ama zemin kat sakinlerini sorar; asansörsüzlükten en az etkilenecek grup üzerinden mantık bağı kopar.

questions.stem: Although the factory was built only ten years ago, it has already been closed twice for safety reasons.

options.o1: The factory is only ten years old, but it has nevertheless had to be shut down twice because of safety concerns.
options.o2: The factory was closed twice for safety reasons before it was completed ten years ago.
options.o3: Safety problems delayed the construction of the factory by about ten years.
options.o4: As the factory is only ten years old, it has never had to be closed for safety reasons.
options.o5: The factory may have to be closed for safety reasons twice in the next ten years.

questions.why: Özgün cümledeki 'Although' karşıtlığı ve iki kez kapanma bilgisi, but ile kurulan bu yeniden yazımda birebir korunur.
questions.trap_note: Karşıtlığı sebebe çevirip cümleyi olumsuzlar; 'rağmen' ile 'diği için' karıştırıldığında anlam tersine döner.

questions.stem: You should have told the office that you were going to be late.

options.o1: It would have been better if you had informed the office about your delay.
options.o2: You must tell the office whenever you are going to be late.
options.o3: The office should be told that you are often late for work.
options.o4: You may have told the office that you were going to be late.
options.o5: There was no need for you to tell the office that you would be late.

questions.why: should have + V3 yapısı, yapılmamış bir eylem için geçmişe yönelik eleştiri bildirir; bunun karşılığı üçüncü tip koşul cümlesidir.
questions.trap_note: Geçmişe yönelik eleştiriyi genel bir kurala çevirir; kip aynı kalsa da zaman ve anlam kayar.

questions.stem: Hardly had the concert begun when the power went off.

options.o1: The electricity failed almost immediately after the concert had started.
options.o2: The concert began as soon as the electricity came back on.
options.o3: The concert could not begin at all because there was no electricity.
options.o4: The power went off shortly before the concert was due to start.
options.o5: The concert went on even though the power had gone off.

questions.why: Hardly ... when devrik yapısı, ilk eylemin hemen ardından ikincisinin gerçekleştiğini bildirir: önce konser başlar, hemen sonra elektrik kesilir.
questions.trap_note: İki olayın sırasını ters çevirir; devrik yapıdaki zaman ilişkisi yanlış yöne okunur.

questions.stem: The new regulation applies to all restaurants except those with fewer than ten tables.

options.o1: Restaurants with ten tables or more are subject to the new regulation.
options.o2: The new regulation applies only to restaurants with fewer than ten tables.
options.o3: All restaurants, including the smallest ones, have to obey the new regulation.
options.o4: Restaurants with exactly ten tables are the only ones exempt from the new regulation.
options.o5: The new regulation will be applied to small restaurants at a later date.

questions.why: 'Onun altında masası olanlar hariç' ifadesi, kuralın on ve daha fazla masası olan işletmeler için geçerli olduğu anlamına gelir.
questions.trap_note: except ile getirilen istisnayı yok sayar; 'all restaurants' ifadesi tek başına okunduğunda kapsam genişletilmiş olur.

questions.stem: Most people believe that a plant grows towards the light because the light attracts it. ---- The cells on the shaded side of the stem grow longer than those on the sunny side, and this difference bends the whole stem in the direction of the light. In other words, the plant is not pulled by the sun; it is pushed by its own uneven growth.

options.o1: In fact, what happens is almost the opposite.
options.o2: Similarly, the roots of a plant grow downwards in search of water.
options.o3: Light, however, is not necessary for most indoor plants.
options.o4: Gardeners therefore water their plants early in the morning.
options.o5: This attraction was first described in the nineteenth century.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonraki açıklama, ilk cümledeki yaygın inanışı çürütür; bu yüzden boşluğa karşıtlık kuran bir geçiş cümlesi gelmelidir.
questions.trap_note: 'This attraction' ile ilk cümledeki yanlış inanışı sürdürür; gönderme yaptığı sözcük doğru olsa da paragrafın yönünü tersine çevirir.

questions.stem: ---- It was originally designed for soldiers who had to read maps at night without being seen, and only later did climbers and cave explorers discover it. Today it is sold in every sports shop, and few walkers set out on a winter afternoon without one in their rucksack.

options.o1: The head torch is a good example of a piece of equipment that has moved from the army into everyday life.
options.o2: Cave exploring became a popular hobby in the second half of the twentieth century.
options.o3: Soldiers today rarely use torches of the kind that were produced in the past.
options.o4: Most walkers now prefer to carry a mobile phone rather than a torch.
options.o5: Reading a map is a skill that is slowly disappearing among young people.

questions.why: Boşluk paragrafın ilk cümlesidir ve sonraki cümlelerdeki 'It' zamirinin göndereni ile konuyu birlikte kurmak zorundadır.
questions.trap_note: Sonraki cümlede geçen mağaracıları öne çıkarır; ancak 'It' zamirine karşılık verecek bir nesne tanıtmaz.

questions.stem: For centuries the people of the Faroe Islands built their houses with roofs of turf. The thick layer of soil and grass kept the heat inside during the long winters and survived winds that would have torn off ordinary tiles. ---- Architects there are now using it again on modern buildings, this time with a waterproof membrane underneath.

options.o1: The technique was almost abandoned when cheap building materials arrived after the war.
options.o2: Therefore, turf roofs have never gone out of fashion on the islands.
options.o3: Moreover, the grass on such a roof has to be cut twice a year.
options.o4: However, ordinary tiles are far cheaper to produce than turf is.
options.o5: These winds are at their strongest in the middle of the summer.

questions.why: Son cümledeki 'using it again' ifadesi, arada tekniğin bir süre bırakıldığını bildiren bir cümle gerektirir.
questions.trap_note: Bağlacın yönü yanlıştır: 'Therefore' ile kurulan bu cümle, 'yeniden kullanıyorlar' ifadesini anlamsız bırakır.

questions.stem: A bicycle is one of the few machines that have hardly changed in a hundred years. The frame, the chain and the two wheels of a modern bike would be recognised at once by a rider from 1920. ---- Gears are shifted electronically, frames are made of carbon fibre, and a small computer records every kilometre. The shape, however, remains the same.

options.o1: That does not mean that nothing about it has been improved.
options.o2: For this reason, most cyclists today prefer much older models.
options.o3: Such riders were far more skilful than today's cyclists are.
options.o4: They are also a good deal cheaper than they used to be.
options.o5: This is why bicycles are no longer produced in Europe.

questions.why: Boşluktan sonra sıralanan yenilikler, 'değişmedi' savını sınırlayan bir geçiş cümlesi gerektirir.
questions.trap_note: 'Such riders' ile bir önceki cümledeki 1920 bisikletlisine gönderme yapar; gönderme doğru görünse de sonraki cümlelerle bağ kurmaz.

sentences: The Finnish city of Lahti gives each of its residents a personal carbon budget for travel.
An app records how they move around the city every day and rewards those who stay below their limit.
The rewards are small - a bus ticket or a cup of coffee - but the number of people using the app has grown every year.
Similar apps are used by runners who want to keep a record of the distance they cover.
City officials say that the scheme works because it turns an abstract idea into a daily choice.
questions.why: IV. cümle uygulamayı bambaşka bir bağlama, koşucuların mesafe ölçümüne taşır; paragrafın konusu olan karbon bütçesiyle ilgisi yoktur.
questions.trap_note: III. cümle ödüllerin küçüklüğünü söylediği için konudan sapıyormuş gibi görünür; oysa 'ama' ile devam ederek katılımın arttığını bildirir ve akışı sürdürür.

sentences: Sourdough bread is made without commercial yeast.
Instead, the baker keeps a mixture of flour and water in which wild yeasts and bacteria live.
This starter has to be fed regularly, rather like a pet.
The long, slow rising that follows gives the bread its sour taste and its open texture.
Most of the bread sold in European supermarkets today is sliced and wrapped in plastic.
questions.why: V. cümle ekmek üretiminden marketteki ambalaja atlar; paragrafın anlattığı ekşi maya sürecini tamamlamaz.
questions.trap_note: III. cümledeki 'evcil hayvan' benzetmesi konu dışı durur; oysa mayanın düzenli beslenmesi sürecin bir adımıdır.

sentences: Lighthouses were once looked after by keepers who lived in them with their families.
The oceans cover more than seventy per cent of the surface of the planet.
Automatic systems replaced almost all of these keepers during the twentieth century.
The last manned lighthouse in Britain was switched to automatic operation in 1998.
Many of the empty buildings have since been turned into small hotels or museums.
questions.why: II. cümle denizlerle ilgili genel bir istatistiktir; paragrafın izlediği deniz feneri bekçiliği tarihine hiçbir katkı yapmaz.
questions.trap_note: V. cümle bekçilerden söz etmediği için kopuk sanılır; oysa boşalan binaların akıbetini anlatarak paragrafı sonuca bağlar.

sentences: Some libraries now lend objects as well as books.
In Toronto, for instance, members can borrow a drill, a tent or a sewing machine for a week.
The first public library in the city was opened in 1883.
The idea is that most households need such items only two or three times a year.
Librarians report that the tool collection is borrowed far more often than the average novel.
questions.why: III. cümle kütüphanenin kuruluş tarihine geçer; paragrafın konusu olan eşya ödünç verme uygulamasını ilerletmez.
questions.trap_note: II. cümle tek bir şehirden söz ettiği için dar görünür; oysa 'for instance' ile ilk cümledeki genel savı örneklendirir.

sentences: Volcanic ash is a serious hazard for aircraft, because it melts inside hot jet engines and can stop them completely.
After the eruption of an Icelandic volcano in 2010, most flights over Europe were cancelled for six days.
Since then, airlines and meteorologists have developed detailed maps showing how thick the ash is at each altitude.
Iceland produces almost all of its electricity from renewable sources such as water and underground heat.
These maps allow aircraft to fly around the dangerous layers instead of grounding the whole fleet.
questions.why: IV. cümle İzlanda'nın enerji üretimine geçer; paragrafın konusu olan kül tehlikesi ve haritalarla ilgisi yoktur.
questions.trap_note: II. cümle tek bir olaya odaklandığı için ayrıntı gibi durur; oysa haritaların neden geliştirildiğini açıklayan olaydır.
